comments.author: @debfranklin6613
comments.text: I lived in the UP in the 1960's, as a child.  I remember going onto Lake Superior and exploring the ice caves, made by the winds and blown spray.  It was magical.  Dangerous, so we were always with a knowledgeable adult, but the silence was deafening inside the frozen water cave.  I went to the John D Pierce Elementary school, which was located on Northern Michigan University campus.  It is no longer there. I remember ice skating every day after school while we waited for our dad to take us home after work.  The cloudiness didn't bother me as a kid because it was all I knew. The Thanksgiving of 1968? snowed us into our lake front home with snow above the doors and windows.  We couldn't get out until we shoveled a tunnel. So many snow forts were built during those years!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What incredible childhood memories! ❤️ Exploring the ice caves of Lake Superior, skating after school while waiting for your father, and digging tunnels through the snow sound like scenes from another world. The silence inside those frozen caves must have been unforgettable. It's amazing how even the harshest winters can become some of our most treasured childhood memories. Thank you so much for sharing such a beautiful glimpse of life in the U.P. during the 1960s. Wishing you good health, happiness, and many more wonderful memories to cherish! ❤️

comments.author: @paulpiasano9251
comments.text: It's spelling would sound like mac in nac island, but it's pronounced mac en naw island. (or mack in awe) When you showed the Grand Hotel, you can add that it is where scenes from the movie Somewhere in Time were filmed. The fudge shops have fans that blow the wonderful smell of the fudge out into the street in front of the shops. St. Ignace is pronounced like saint ig nas. It's not just the locals who pronounce the city Sue St. Marie, that is the correct pronounciation. Pasties are a mainstay in the UP.  The late Gordon Lightfoot wrote a song about the wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald in Lake Superior. Houghton is pronounced hoe-tun. Really enjoyed the video about Poland, and have never been there, but I have been to most of the places in this video, and have gone to the island and St. Ignace since the 60s.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Thank you so much for sharing these wonderful details and personal memories! It's especially lovely to hear from someone who has been visiting Mackinac Island and St. Ignace since the 1960s. Your insights into the local pronunciations, the Grand Hotel, the fudge shops, and the region's history are truly appreciated. We'll certainly pay closer attention to the pronunciations in future videos. We're also delighted that you enjoyed our documentary about Poland! Wishing you good health, happiness, and many more beautiful memories of Michigan's Upper Peninsula. ❤️
